name: komdosh-claude-developer
description: Backend and infrastructure engineering for Claude Code — 8 composable plugins. Four for Kotlin + Spring (core implementation, quality audits, delivery and release, knowledge retrieval) plus kotlin-extras for niche maintenance; three for infrastructure (shared safety and data-protection discipline, Terraform with Yandex Cloud, Kubernetes with ArgoCD). Every auditor is read-only at the tool layer; nothing applies, deploys, syncs, or publishes on its own.

plugins.name: komdosh-dev-spring-core
plugins.description: The foundation for Kotlin + Spring WebFlux services: implementing, verifying, and reviewing code inside one service — including its Kafka/SQS consumers and Avro schemas, which answer to the same hexagonal and coroutine rules. Enforces the 12 forbidden coroutine patterns, hexagonal module boundaries, RFC 9457 errors, application-layer PII handling, consumer idempotency and DLQ policy, and Avro schema/registry discipline. Grep-based preflight skills catch the mechanical violations in seconds, before a full Gradle cycle.

plugins.name: komdosh-dev-spring-quality
plugins.description: Audits and QA artifacts on top of spring-core. Finds out what is actually true about a finished service: which routes are unauthenticated, what leaks through error bodies, whether JWT validation is real, where personal data escapes in logs and events, and which vendor types have leaked into application code. Also generates the QA artifacts a human tester needs — a validation checklist, a Newman-runnable Postman collection, and a self-contained HTML console — from one API-surface discovery. Read-only on the audit side: never edits, never extracts a secret, never prints personal data. Requires komdosh-dev-spring-core.

plugins.name: komdosh-dev-spring-delivery
plugins.description: Everything between 'a ticket exists' and 'the release PR is open'. Pulls work in from Jira, turns an architecture package into ordered agent todos, computes a lifecycle gate map from real git state and recommends the next action, and runs two-track release engineering — services get a rollback playbook, libraries get an ABI-load-bearing version bump. Never deploys, never pushes a tag, never merges a PR. Requires komdosh-dev-spring-core.

plugins.name: komdosh-dev-revealer
plugins.description: Retrieval before invention. /reveal surfaces what the project already decided — ADRs, specs, plans, decision comments, commit archaeology, and any RAG/MCP knowledge base wired up. /doc-reveal finds real documentation for a symbol or library, cheapest source first (in-repo KDoc, project docs, cache, MCP, canonical web docs, jar listings, decompilation last) and caches the result. Both cite their source and name the gaps instead of filling them; a gap is a result, an invented citation is the failure. Requires komdosh-dev-spring-core.

plugins.name: komdosh-dev-kotlin-extras
plugins.description: Niche maintenance tooling on top of spring-core — install only if you need one. /upgrade bumps one library at a time with the changelog's breaking changes mapped to the files they affect. /detect-flakes re-runs tests until it can classify each as deterministic or flaky, with evidence. /load-test-new scaffolds a Gatling simulation. Each surfaces and classifies; the specialists fix. Requires komdosh-dev-spring-core.

plugins.name: komdosh-dev-infra-core
plugins.description: The foundation for infrastructure-as-code and GitOps: the shared safety, secrets, promotion, and data-protection discipline the other infra plugins build on. Every action obeys one contract — render the desired state, review the blast radius, apply only the reviewed artifact. Three read-only agents review a change across six dimensions, hunt exposed secrets across every layer, and audit personal data across the infrastructure lifecycle under both 152-FZ and GDPR. Read-only at the tool layer, not merely by convention. No cloud or language assumptions.

plugins.name: komdosh-dev-infra-iac
plugins.description: Terraform and OpenTofu authoring, plan-safety analysis, and state discipline, with the Yandex Cloud resource layer built in. One agent writes and one reviews, and they never overlap. The reviewer anchors on the plan rather than the source, because destroys and replaces hide there — an additive-looking diff can produce a forced replacement that destroys a database. Secure-and-HA by default on YC: regional K8s masters, HA managed databases with backups, Lockbox and KMS, least-privilege IAM, and 152-FZ data residency. Never runs apply or destroy. Requires komdosh-dev-infra-core.

plugins.name: komdosh-dev-infra-k8s
plugins.description: Kubernetes manifests, hardening, workload troubleshooting, and ArgoCD delivery. Three agents with disjoint verbs — author, auditor, diagnostician — split by what you are doing rather than which tool, so a Deployment and the Application that ships it stay one change. Author and auditor work on the rendered manifest, because an overlay can silently drop a hardening patch the base contains. The diagnostician separates sync status from health status and refuses workarounds that hide a symptom. Never mutates a cluster; rollback is git revert. Requires komdosh-dev-infra-core.
